limitations: Knowledge-area coverage is not lifecycle-process or standards-clause conformity.
required_behavior: Record every applicable knowledge area, justified exclusions, owners, and evidence homes.
entries.synthesis: Use the knowledge-area map to locate missing requirements, architecture, design, construction, verification, operation, maintenance, configuration, management, process, quality, security, economics, and foundation work.
entries.title: Check the whole software-engineering discipline surface

limitations: The exact Ranex process and authority model come from accepted lifecycle controls, not this guide alone.
required_behavior: Bind changed requirements to decisions, implementation, tests, release evidence, and maintenance consequences.
entries.synthesis: Treat requirements, design, construction, testing, configuration, maintenance, quality, and management as connected disciplines with explicit trace and change control.
entries.title: Trace engineering work through change and quality evidence

limitations: Iterative design does not authorize authority, security, persistence, or recovery decisions to emerge accidentally.
required_behavior: Record local design alternatives and re-enter material discoveries through normal design/change control.
entries.synthesis: Treat construction design as iterative, heuristic, tradeoff-bearing work that may reveal facts requiring controlled design revision.
entries.title: Perform explicit, proportionate design during construction

limitations: Simplicity cannot omit essential authority, denial, failure, recovery, or lifecycle behavior.
required_behavior: Name essential complexity and show how the chosen design removes or contains accidental complexity.
entries.synthesis: Make required domain and failure complexity explicit while reducing incidental coupling, duplication, and mechanism leakage.
entries.title: Separate essential from accidental complexity

limitations: This principle does not prove any particular bounded-context count or directory tree.

locators.section: Chapter 5, information hiding, cohesion, coupling, and interfaces

required_behavior: Assign one owner, expose a narrow contract, and prevent consumers from depending on the hidden mechanism.
entries.synthesis: Decompose around owned responsibilities, conceal change-prone mechanisms, and minimize coupling through explicit interfaces and contracts.
entries.title: Hide volatile decisions behind cohesive interfaces

limitations: A wrapper is not sufficient evidence for security, protocol correctness, or operational recovery.
required_behavior: Expose an owned port, translate external types, and test the adapter contract and failure paths.
entries.synthesis: Keep vendor and external API concepts outside core policy by translating them through owned boundary contracts.
entries.title: Wrap volatile and third-party interfaces

limitations: Dependency-injection style is a means, not the control objective.

locators.section: Chapter 11, separating constructing a system from using it

required_behavior: Keep dependency assembly at the composition boundary and reject import-time or environment-presence authority selection.
entries.synthesis: Confine configuration discovery, object assembly, and startup wiring so runtime policy receives validated dependencies instead of discovering global mechanisms.
entries.title: Separate system construction from runtime policy

limitations: Local cleanliness cannot compensate for a failed architecture, security, or lifecycle gate.
required_behavior: Keep scope bounded and preserve all applicable tests and trace evidence through each refactoring step.
entries.synthesis: Improve local clarity, cohesion, and duplication only while preserving requirement and regression evidence.
entries.title: Refactor in small verified steps

limitations: DRY must not create shared domain ownership, a common database, or a god service.
required_behavior: Name the semantic owner and generate or validate every duplicate representation against it.
entries.synthesis: Eliminate duplicated knowledge by generating or projecting representations from one accepted semantic owner.
entries.title: Keep authoritative knowledge in one governed source

limitations: Perfect independence is neither possible nor required; necessary coupling must remain explicit.
required_behavior: Declare dependencies and demonstrate that representative changes do not spread through unrelated owners.
entries.synthesis: Design components so a change in one concern has a small, explicit effect on unrelated concerns.
entries.title: Localize the effect of change

limitations: Optionality has cost and must be proportionate to a named uncertainty.
required_behavior: Record lock-in, exit conditions, migration path, rollback limits, and retirement consequences.
entries.synthesis: Delay avoidable lock-in and design migrations, rollback, and retirement before committing to volatile mechanisms.
entries.title: Preserve viable options and reversal paths

limitations: A tracer is not an MVP scope decision, disposable prototype, or permission to leave authority and interfaces undefined.
required_behavior: Route through production-shaped interfaces, capture falsification evidence, and retain the mapped destination and missing coverage explicitly.
entries.synthesis: Build a narrow end-to-end route that exercises real boundaries and yields feedback without treating the route as the complete product.
entries.title: Use production-shaped tracer routes for learning

limitations: Interview time boxes are not Ranex policy and the method does not prove completeness by itself.

locators.section: A 4-step process for effective system design

required_behavior: Record actors, requirements, scale envelope, complete decomposition, selected deep dives, tradeoffs, and unresolved questions.
entries.synthesis: Structure architecture work by clarifying scope and quality needs, mapping the whole high-level system, selecting risk-bearing seams for deep analysis, and reconciling tradeoffs and remaining unknowns.
entries.title: Clarify, decompose, deep-dive, and reconcile

limitations: Simplified interview examples and missing extraction figures are insufficient decision evidence.

locators.section: Scale estimation and high-level design pattern catalogue

required_behavior: Bind a measured load/failure need, consistency model, operating cost, recovery design, and accepted ADR before adoption.
entries.synthesis: Use cache, queue, replication, sharding, rate limiting, and multi-region patterns as questions to investigate, not defaults.
entries.title: Require measured need before adopting scale patterns

limitations: Examples clarify requirements; they do not replace the requirements, risks, or human decision.
required_behavior: Bind executable examples to owned requirements and preserve independent acceptance authority.
entries.synthesis: Clarify expected behavior with accountable stakeholders using examples that remain traceable to requirements and independent acceptance.
entries.title: Co-develop executable acceptance examples

limitations: The book's fixed pyramid percentages and coverage figures are rejected as universal gates.
required_behavior: Map each material risk to the lowest-cost convincing evidence and retain required integration, security, resilience, and operational proof.
entries.synthesis: Combine local, component, integration, system, acceptance, and exploratory evidence according to the subject's failure modes.
entries.title: Use multiple verification levels selected by risk

limitations: Heroic certainty, overtime, and fixed estimation mechanics are not acceptable substitutes for evidence.
required_behavior: Record forecast range, assumptions, dependencies, capacity authority, risk disclosure, and recommitment triggers.
entries.synthesis: Express forecasts as uncertainty and commit only to controlled actions, named dependencies, and explicit recommitment conditions.
entries.title: Separate uncertainty estimates from commitments

limitations: The local copy's Chapter 1 does not supply Ranex security, privacy, release, or management controls.

locators.section: Chapter 1, Reliable, Scalable and Maintainable Applications

required_behavior: Define faults, load parameters, performance distributions, operational needs, and evolvability evidence for the exact subject.
entries.synthesis: Translate broad quality labels into fault behavior, quantified load/performance measures, operability, complexity control, and evolvability.
entries.title: Define reliability, scalability, and maintainability operationally

limitations: Monotonic clocks do not make lease ownership safe after process pauses.
required_behavior: Specify the clock source for timestamps, deadlines, elapsed durations, and cross-host comparisons.
entries.synthesis: Separate wall-clock timestamps from elapsed-duration measurement and do not compare host-local monotonic values across machines.
entries.title: Use monotonic time for elapsed-duration decisions

limitations: The cited model assumes unreliable but honest nodes; authentication, authorization, sandboxing, and hostile-worker controls remain separate.

locators.section: Chapter 8, process pauses and fencing tokens

required_behavior: Bind every protected write, tool, budget, mailbox, and external-effect sink to an epoch check enforced beyond the worker.
entries.synthesis: Issue monotonically increasing epochs and require the state/effect sink itself to reject stale epochs; client-side lease checks are insufficient.
entries.title: Fence stale workers at every protected resource

limitations: CDC mechanisms and distributed brokers are examples, not required Ranex technologies.

locators.section: Chapter 11, keeping systems in sync and change data capture

required_behavior: Name the system of record, local atomic boundary, event order, duplicate policy, consumer lag, replay, and reconciliation.
entries.synthesis: Commit canonical state and a durable change record atomically where possible, then treat downstream views and consumers as ordered, replayable, lagging derivations.
entries.title: Avoid ungoverned dual writes

limitations: The source's retain-all-events assumption can conflict with privacy, legal, and bounded-retention obligations.

locators.section: Chapter 11, event sourcing and state derivation

required_behavior: Specify validation, event acceptance, deterministic projection, snapshot authority, replay, consistency, retention, correction, and erasure behavior.
entries.synthesis: Validate a command before accepting it as a durable event, and make state derivation deterministic with explicit snapshot, replay, retention, and deletion rules.
entries.title: Distinguish proposed commands from accepted immutable events

limitations: Do not claim end-to-end exactly-once behavior from a local idempotency mechanism.
required_behavior: Define operation identity, duplicate detection scope, atomic boundary, retry lifetime, non-idempotent effect handling, and reconciliation owner.
entries.synthesis: Use stable operation identities and atomicity or idempotence to make retries safe, while explicitly reconciling effects that cannot be naturally repeated.
entries.title: State exact retry and idempotency assumptions

limitations: A named architecture style does not supply the missing characteristics or rationale.
required_behavior: Bind each material structural choice to named characteristics, decisions, principles, and stakeholder outcomes.
entries.synthesis: A topology is incomplete without explicit quality characteristics, decision rationale, and governing design principles.
entries.title: Define architecture through structure, characteristics, decisions, and principles

limitations: A proxy count or one-time document check is not proof of sustained effectiveness.
required_behavior: For each material characteristic, define the metric or invariant, threshold/distribution, subject, cadence, owner, and response to failure.
entries.synthesis: Turn important architecture characteristics into observable constraints or tests that detect drift and falsify assumptions.
entries.title: Govern characteristics with subject-specific fitness functions

limitations: Generic style ratings do not substitute for Ranex measurements and priorities.

locators.section: Laws of Software Architecture and least-worst architecture

required_behavior: Compare status quo and at least one viable alternative, including benefits, costs, failure modes, reversibility, and falsifiers.
entries.synthesis: Compare viable alternatives against the exact quality priorities and retain why the selected compromise fits better than the alternatives.
entries.title: Record the least-worst contextual tradeoff

limitations: More components or bounded contexts do not automatically mean better modularity.

locators.section: Components, architecture quanta, and boundary tradeoffs

required_behavior: Measure coupling and communication across every proposed boundary and justify its consistency, failure, ownership, and change-locality benefit.
entries.synthesis: Choose component granularity and transactional/communication boundaries from characteristics and coupling, then revisit them as evidence changes.
entries.title: Justify component and consistency boundaries

limitations: Central authority can be necessary; the risk is unbounded responsibility and knowledge, not centrality by itself.
required_behavior: Measure the central component's responsibility set, dependency fan-in/fan-out, change coupling, and cross-boundary communication.
entries.synthesis: Separate necessary consistency authority from business and technical orchestration responsibilities, and detect excessive central knowledge or communication.
entries.title: Keep orchestration from becoming a coupling hub

limitations: The source's qualitative star tables are prompts, not a Ranex scoring model.

locators.section: Choosing an architecture style and modular monolith

required_behavior: Use synchronous interaction by default inside the local product unless async has a measured benefit, and record every significant exception with alternatives and fitness evidence.
entries.synthesis: Choose topology and interaction style from domain, characteristics, data, organization, and process, then capture context, alternatives, decision, consequences, and compliance evidence.
entries.title: Select style contextually and record significant decisions

limitations: Use-case visibility does not prove that one package layout or one object model is universally correct.
required_behavior: Ensure top-level ownership and APIs communicate Ranex capabilities and keep delivery mechanisms outside domain policy.
entries.synthesis: Organize core policy around owned use cases and domain intent rather than delivery frameworks or technical mechanisms.
entries.title: Make product intent visible in the architecture

limitations: A boundary has cost; do not create it solely because the book names a mechanism a detail.

locators.section: Chapter 16, Leaving Options Open; Chapter 17, Boundaries and Plugin Architecture

required_behavior: Name the policy protected, volatile decision deferred, boundary cost, allowed dependencies, and change/failure tests.
entries.synthesis: Separate policy from volatile UI, database, framework, and provider choices where the expected change and quality benefit justify the boundary.
entries.title: Draw boundaries to protect policy and preserve options

limitations: The rule must be reconciled with language, performance, data ownership, and operational constraints rather than applied ceremonially.
required_behavior: Prevent inner policy from importing outer mechanisms or their generated data formats; translate at the boundary.
entries.synthesis: Make dependencies point from replaceable delivery and infrastructure mechanisms toward stable application/domain policy through owned abstractions and translated data.
entries.title: Keep mechanism dependencies outside policy

limitations: Neither a monolith nor a service topology is automatically well-architected.
required_behavior: Demonstrate policy boundary, independent failure/change benefit, communication semantics, and operating cost before splitting a process.
entries.synthesis: Judge a service or component boundary by policy separation, dependencies, ownership, change, and failure behavior rather than deployment process count.
entries.title: Do not equate process separation with architecture

limitations: The source's test API may bypass security for tests; Ranex must isolate that capability so it cannot exist as a production bypass.

locators.section: Chapter 34, Package by Component and Organization versus Encapsulation

required_behavior: Restrict internal visibility, expose purpose-specific public and test contracts, and prevent test-only bypass from becoming production authority.
entries.synthesis: Use language visibility and testing interfaces so declared components actually hide internals and business behavior can be tested without volatile delivery mechanisms.
entries.title: Make boundaries enforceable in code and tests

limitations: The three symptoms are qualitative diagnostic lenses, not an additive or universal architecture score; unfamiliar-reader results depend on subject, task, and reviewer.
required_behavior: Identify expected change paths, dependencies, facts a maintainer must know, and obscured behavior; require both change-impact evidence and an independent unfamiliar-reader omission challenge.
entries.synthesis: Treat change amplification, cognitive load, and unknown unknowns as distinct symptoms of dependency and obscurity, then test whether a proposed design contains rather than merely relocates them.
entries.title: Detect complexity through its change and comprehension symptoms

limitations: Depth is a contextual relationship, not a mandate to maximize module size; god modules, excessive responsibility, authority ambiguity, and hidden failure behavior remain prohibited.
required_behavior: Justify each material module, bounded context, and optional layer by the useful complexity it hides and the burden its public interface imposes on consumers; merge or remove shallow indirection without creating unbounded owners.
entries.synthesis: Make public interfaces simple, stable, and complete relative to the useful functionality and volatile decisions hidden behind them, while avoiding shallow layer or class proliferation.
entries.title: Prefer modules whose interfaces hide substantial useful complexity
verification_methods: public API surface and consumer analysis

limitations: Information hiding cannot conceal facts required for authority, denial, security, audit, failure, recovery, or operation; those facts need explicit contracts and evidence.
required_behavior: Assign one semantic owner to each material design decision, expose a narrow complete contract, and test that consumers cannot depend on hidden representation, mechanism, ordering, or lifecycle details.
entries.synthesis: Localize knowledge of volatile formats, mechanisms, ordering, policy, and failure behavior behind an owned interface, and reject information leakage or temporal decomposition that spreads one decision across modules.
entries.title: Hide each design decision under one semantic owner

limitations: The effort must be proportionate to decision significance and uncertainty; trivial or readily reversible local choices do not require ceremonial alternatives.
required_behavior: For each significant architecture decision, compare the status quo and at least two viable shapes, record their costs, failure modes, reversibility, interface burden, and falsifiers, and retain accountable decision authority.
entries.synthesis: Before fixing a consequential interface, boundary, or mechanism, sketch more than one viable design and compare interface burden, information hiding, change impact, failure behavior, and quality-attribute consequences.
entries.title: Compare multiple designs for significant decisions
